title: A blocked model host must be a readable error, not an error loop (1.3.1)
description: User 'micha' (Win11, v1.3.0 portable on D:) hit 100% failure on every models.cubric.studio download (44 attempts, 0 successes, each dead in <200ms with TLS WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER) while all 45 github.com downloads succeeded - his network is intercepting our model host. The install and the D: portable layout are fine. Three app defects turned that recoverable condition into an unrecoverable error loop: (1) the raw BoringSSL string is surfaced verbatim with no hostname or remedy, and the same failure also escapes as an unhandled promise rejection; (2) installStore makes FAILED terminal so the deliberate failed->queued retry requeue is rejected, leaving the UI read path stuck on failed while downloads actually run - this breaks retry for EVERY user after any transient failure; (3) app.getPath('documents') throwing at main.js:637 hard-exits the app at boot even though routes/shared.js already has a fallback. Target 1.3.1. A fallback mirror hostname is the durable fix but is an approval-gated Cloudflare change - see brief.md.
